# Shared device MIB and extended OID options

`snmp_mib.py` defines **182 object types** shared by the Agent and Manager. The
Manager's numbered catalog has **180 choices**, retaining the original 1–25
numbers and adding the extended entries. Indexed objects produce one instance
per interface, process, filesystem, disk, sensor, or service.

## Explore the clean MIB tree

```bash
./snmp_data_collector_v12.py mib
./snmp_data_collector_v12.py mib --group storage
./snmp_data_collector_v12.py mib --group processes
./snmp_agent.py mib --group sensors
```

Both programs render the same tree. Entries show a symbol, numeric branch,
data type, collection group, units, writable status, and optional availability.
Use `--root .1.3.6.1.2.1.25` to focus on HOST-RESOURCES-MIB, for example.

Main branches:

```text
internet (.1.3.6.1)
|-- mgmt / mib-2 (.1.3.6.1.2.1)
|   |-- system: description, hostname, contact, location, agent uptime
|   |-- interfaces / ifMIB: names, type, MAC, MTU, speed, status, counters
|   |-- ip: IPv4 addresses, interface indexes, netmasks
|   |-- tcp: established/CLOSE_WAIT connection count
|   `-- hostResources
|       |-- hrSystem: host uptime, logged-in sessions, process count
|       |-- hrStorage: RAM, swap, and accessible mounted filesystems
|       |-- hrProcessorLoad: per-logical-CPU load
|       `-- hrSWRun / hrSWRunPerf: process identity, status, CPU time, RAM
`-- private / enterprises (.1.3.6.1.4.1)
    |-- ucdSnmpAgent (2021): memory, load averages, CPU idle, disk I/O
    `-- hookah (32473.1)
        |-- packetMetrics: total RX/TX packet counters
        |-- collectionControl: settings and collection timing/counts
        `-- deviceMetrics (4)
            |-- hostInformation (1)
            |-- memoryDetails (2)
            |-- cpuDetails (3)
            |-- storageAndDiskIO (4)
            |-- processMetrics (5)
            |-- connectionSummary (6)
            |-- sensors (7)
            |-- networkAddresses (8)
            `-- windowsServices (9)
```

The complete numeric tree is generated by the commands above; the displayed
summary is abbreviated. Enterprise number 32473 is reserved for documentation
and examples, matching the existing lab Agent.

## Display what a device actually exposes

```bash
./snmp_data_collector_v12.py browse --target udp:192.168.1.20:1161 \
  --community public --group storage --output filesystems.csv

./snmp_data_collector_v12.py browse --target udp:192.168.1.20:1161 \
  --community public --group processes

./snmp_data_collector_v12.py mib --target udp:192.168.1.20:1161 \
  --community public --group cpu
```

`browse` prints available instances with readable names, units, descriptions,
and their exact OIDs. Counter snapshots are identified as cumulative counters;
use `capture` to calculate their rates. Add the existing `--encryption-config`
option for an encrypted Agent.

On the monitored device:

```bash
./snmp_agent.py mib --config snmp_agent_config.json --group storage --values
./snmp_agent.py --list-oids
```

Use WALK/browse to discover indexes, then supply the index when selecting an
indexed catalog entry. Interface indexes are native when available; disk,
filesystem, address, sensor, and service indexes remain stable while the Agent
runs. Process indexes are actual PIDs. RAM remains storage index **1**, swap is
**2**, and filesystem storage rows begin at **3**.

## Collection groups and measurements

| Group | Measurements |
| --- | --- |
| `system` | OS name/release/version, architecture, processor/Python description, boot time, host/agent uptime, user sessions, process count. |
| `interfaces` | Description, link type, MAC, MTU, speed, admin/oper state, state-change time, packet/error/discard counters, IPv4/IPv6 address details. |
| `ifInOctets`, `ifOutOctets` | 32-bit and high-capacity 64-bit traffic counters, converted to Mbps by the Manager. |
| `cpu` | Logical/physical core counts, rolling core load/idle, current/min/max MHz, interval CPU-time category percentages, context-switch/interrupt/syscall counters. |
| `memory` | Total/available/free/used RAM, buffers/cache/active/inactive RAM where provided, utilization, swap total/used/free/percent. |
| `load` | One-, five-, and fifteen-minute load averages where supported. |
| `storage` | Mount point, device, filesystem type/options, total/used/free bytes, utilization, HOST-RESOURCES allocation units. |
| `diskio` | Per-device 32/64-bit read/write bytes and operations, elapsed read/write/busy milliseconds, merged operations where available. |
| `processes` | PID/parent PID, name, executable, owner/status, threads, CPU utilization/time, RSS and virtual memory. |
| `connections` | TCP totals and ESTABLISHED/LISTEN/TIME_WAIT/CLOSE_WAIT/SYN_SENT counts, UDP socket count. |
| `sensors` | Battery percent/power/time, temperature current/high/critical, fan RPM where exposed. |
| `services` | Windows service name/display/status/startup/PID/account/description/binary path. |

All groups support the existing numeric-second configuration interface:

```bash
./snmp_agent.py config set --config snmp_agent_config.json \
  --interval processes 10 --interval sensors 5 --interval diskio 1
```

Optional OS APIs and permissions determine which instances are present. Missing
information is omitted rather than replaced by artificial zero readings. The
Manager tree lists optional definitions; live `browse` shows actual values.
Windows service inventory is Windows-specific; temperatures/fans depend on
hardware/OS support. Per-process CPU percent can exceed 100% on multiple cores.

Large/fractional non-counter gauges use numeric OCTET STRINGs. Shared metadata
lets the Manager distinguish them from cumulative counters and convert byte
gauges to GiB. Disk byte counters become MiB/s; network byte counters become Mbps.
Sensor thresholds absent from the OS are omitted. The portable backend exposes
total packets separately and retains unicast-only catalog entries for external
agents that can provide them.

## Help and options

```bash
./snmp_data_collector_v12.py help
./snmp_data_collector_v12.py help capture
./snmp_data_collector_v12.py help keys generate
./snmp_data_collector_v12.py catalog
./snmp_agent.py help
./snmp_agent.py help config set
```

In the Manager's interactive menu, type `help`, `h`, or `?`. Option **10** displays
the MIB tree and **11** browses named device metrics. CLI commands also include
`get`, `walk`, `set`, `capture`, `browse`, `mib`, `catalog`, `plot`, `compare`, and
`keys generate`; each help topic describes its flags and behavior.
